scope: ArcPts, SegN, ClampK and RaySegments helpers plus travelled-curvature main branch; remaining geometry consumers remain separately scoped
rangesReviewed: 2519-2555 travelled curvature, direction reset and bend length
450-554 complete Sense body; classifier and gate helpers retain separately scoped reviews
sourceIntent: Predict obstacle rays along measured travelled curvature only for a short bend horizon, then continue tangentially. Bound bend angle and segment work; reset curvature after standing or changing forward/reverse direction.
sourceMechanics: ArcPts bends only through BendLen and then extends straight along the reached tangent.
SegN chooses one to three segments using bend angle and ray length; ClampK limits the bent part to about seventy degrees.
RaySegments converts the model arc to fixed height above local ground; this is an observation path, not native steering execution.
The main branch derives curvature as 2*x/(x*x+y*y) from old position in current model space, with three-metre/1.5-second measurement thresholds and a 250m straightness radius.
waitComparison: DrivingTurnTrack already uses travelled curvature with owner/context/seat binding, freshness and direction/standing reset.
DrivingGeometryCap already bounds the near bend horizon and continues tangentially. Physical sweep adequacy and grade/bridge behaviour remain unaccepted.

DrivingNativePathWatch additionally observes native driver PathCalculated events; it grants no movement or clearance authority. A next-three-node window could reject dense valid forward nodes before they span three metres.

The revised native hint walks six metres of retained path distance, interpolates sparse segments, preserves floor/forward/disconnected-stretch guards and makes at most two bounded passes over the existing 64 nodes.
limits: No new world query, movement command or scheduler was added by this hint change.
Retaining only the first 64 event nodes can still leave a vehicle without usable nearby evidence.
A current native path is a hint, not proof of collision clearance, physical steering, progress or mission completion.
Dense/sparse paths, stopped turns, grades, repeated native orders, interruption and the runtime performance budget need physical acceptance.

sensingExtension.sourceIntent: Sense casts a ground-relative low row through curved segments, classifies hits and evaluates lateral distance along the arc/tangent. STRICT sensing narrows bypass treatment of the excluded object. Debug publication is throttled.
sensingExtension.comparison: WAIT samples rigid body rows at current absolute elevation and retains separate gate, traffic and pedestrian observers. This review found its solid filter used absolute normal Z even though only upward support should be excluded.
sensingExtension.change: Use signed normal Z for support exclusion. Downward underside hits remain solid constraints. Ray count, observation cadence and native movement authority are unchanged.
sensingExtension.engineContract: The second element of each returned intersection is the intersected surface normal. GEOM sensing is not a complete PhysX or hull-clearance proof.
sensingExtension.remaining: Source classifier/gate adapters are separately reviewed. Terrain-relative low rows versus absolute body rows, grade/deck transitions, modded undersides and physical braking still require measured comparison.
